## Lists...
```{r}
l = list(
  vec_numeric = 5:17,
  mat = matrix(1:8, nrow = 2, ncol = 4, byrow = TRUE),
  vec_logical = c(TRUE),
  summary_table = summary(rnorm(1000))
)

# 2 brackets pull something out of a list
l[[1]]
l[[2]]
l[["vec_logical"]]
```
## 'for' loops

```{r}
list_norm = list(
  a = rnorm(20, 3, 4),
    b = rnorm(20, -14, 20),
    c = rnorm(20, 1000, 1000),
    d = rnorm(20, 0, 1)
)

list_norm

```

Can I get mean and SD for each sample?
```{r}
mean_and_sd(list_norm[[1]])
mean_and_sd(list_norm[[2]])
mean_and_sd(list_norm[[3]])
mean_and_sd(list_norm[[4]])

# this is good, but can lose track of these
```

Can I do better?
```{r}
output = vector("list", length = 4)
# creating a list called output with a length of 4
for (i in 1:4) {
  
  output[[i]] = mean_and_sd(list_norm[[i]])
  
}

output
```
## 'map' instead

This is better!
```{r}
output = map(list_norm, mean_and_sd)

# i think this one is not giving a list and it giving dfs instead bc the mean_and_sd function tells it to output a df

output = map(list_norm, median)

# map(input list, function you want to apply)

# map gives a list
```
What about map variants
```{r}
output = map_dbl(list_norm, median)
# makes it a vector 

output = map_df(list_norm, median)
# makes it a data frame
```
## List columns

Time to make some list columns!!!
```{r}
listcol_df = 
  tibble(
    name = c("a", "b", "c", "d"),
    samp = list_norm
  )

# makes it so the values of the "samp" variable within the df are lists
listcol_df
```
Do stuff with this
```{r}
listcol_df |> 
  filter(name %in% c("a", "b", "c", "d"))

listcol_df |> 
  pull(samp)
# look at the lists
```
What about mean and sd
```{r}
mean_and_sd(pull(listcol_df, samp)[[1]])
# applies mean and sd function to the first list in the samp variable in the listcol_df data frame
```
Could I iterate?
```{r}
map(pull(listcol_df, samp), mean_and_sd)
#in this case, the input list is being pulled out of the listcol_df data frame
```

This is where it gets really cool
```{r}
listcol_df |> 
  mutate(
    output = map(samp, mean_and_sd)
  )

# across the lists in the samp variable, apply mean and sd function

listcol_df |> 
  mutate(
    output = map_df(samp, mean_and_sd)
  )


listcol_df |> 
  mutate(
    output = map_dbl(samp, median)
  )
# need map_dbl here instead of just map because it kinda takes the numbers out of the list so you can see them

```
```{r}
nsduh_url = "https://www.samhsa.gov/data/sites/default/files/NSDUHsaeShortTermCHG2015/NSDUHsaeShortTermCHG2015.htm"
nsduh_html = read_html(nsduh_url)

nsduh_process(html = nsduh_html, table_num = 1)
nsduh_process(html = nsduh_html, table_num = 4)
nsduh_process(html = nsduh_html, table_num = 5)
```

Import using iteration
```{r}
output = vector("list", length =3)

table_nums = c(1, 4, 5)

for (i in 1:3) {
  output[[i]] = nsduh_process(html = nsduh_html, table_num = table_nums[i])
}

output
# table numbers 1, 4, and 5 indexed by 1:3
```

Let's build up a map example
```{r}
output = map(table_nums, nsduh_process, html = nsduh_html)

# what you are mapping across, the function, then additional arguments the function needs
```

Let's try list columns!
```{r}
nsduh_df = 
  tibble(
    drug = c("marj", "cocaine", "heroin"),
    num = c(1, 4, 5)
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    table = map(num, nsduh_process, html = nsduh_html)
  ) |> 
  select(-num) |> 
  unnest(table)
# unnest takes sub data frames and expands them out

nsduh_df |> 
  filter(age == "12-17") |> 
  mutate(State = fct_reorder(State, percent)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = State, y = percent, color = year))+
  geom_point()+
  facet_grid(.~drug)


```

## Weather again?
```{r}
data("weather_df")

weather_df =
  weather_df |> 
  nest(data = date:tmin)
```
What if i want to do a regression of tmax on tmin for each station?
```{r}
lm(tmax ~ tmin, data = pull(weather_df, data)[[1]])
lm(tmax ~ tmin, data = pull(weather_df, data)[[2]])
lm(tmax ~ tmin, data = pull(weather_df, data)[[3]])

weather_lm = function(input_data){
  lm(tmax~tmin, data = input_data)
}
# this is a function

weather_lm(pull(weather_df, data)[[1]])

weather_df |> 
  mutate(
    lm_fits = map(data, weather_lm)
  ) |> 
  pull(lm_fits)
```
